findings.description: The removed block normalized a path_url starting with "//" to a single leading slash before it was passed to urllib3. With it gone, a request path_url like "//foo" is handed to urllib3.urlopen unchanged.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a request to a URL such as http://host//evil.com/path, so path_url is "//evil.com/path". urllib3 treats a url starting with "//" as a scheme-relative reference and can parse "evil.com" as the host. The request may then be sent to the wrong target or fail. Unless the commit also changes path_url or urllib3 handling elsewhere, which is not visible in this diff, the guard is lost with no replacement.
